The 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League was the second season of the UEFA Europa Conference League, Europe's tertiary club football tournament organised by UEFA.

The final was played at Fortuna Arena in Prague, Czech Republic.[3] It was won by West Ham United, who defeated Fiorentina 2–1, and qualified for the 2023–24 UEFA Europa League group stage as a result.[4]

As the title holders, Roma qualified for the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League. They were unable to defend their title after advancing to the Europa League knockout phase.

Association team allocationedit

A total of 177 teams from 54 of the 55 UEFA member associations (excluding Russia) participated in the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League. The association ranking based on the UEFA country coefficients was used to determine the number of participating teams for each association:[5]

Associations 1–5 each had one team qualify.
Associations 6–17 (except Russia)[Note RUS] and 51–55 each had two teams qualify.
Associations 18–50 (except Liechtenstein)[Note LIE] each had three teams qualify.
Liechtenstein had one team qualify as they organized only a domestic cup and no domestic league.[Note LIE]
Moreover, 18 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Champions League and 25 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League were transferred to the Europa Conference League.
Association rankingedit

For the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League, the associations were allocated places according to their 2021 UEFA country coefficients, which took into account their performance in European competitions from 2016–17 to 2020–21.[6]

Apart from the allocation based on the country coefficients, associations could have additional teams participating in the Europa Conference League, as noted below:

(UCL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Champions League
(UEL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Europa League

Distributionedit

The following was the access list for this season.[7] In the default access list, the title holders of the Europa Conference League qualified for the Europa League group stage.

Due to the suspension of Russia for the 2022–23 European season, the following changes to the access list were made:

The cup winners of association 16 (Serbia) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 18 (Croatia) and 19 (Switzerland) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 30 to 39 (Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republic of Ireland, North Macedonia and Armenia) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Since several changes were made in the Europa League access list following the qualification of the Europa Conference League title holders to the Europa League group stage, the following changes to the access list were made:

The cup winners of association 17 (Czech Republic) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of association 20 (Greece) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 40 (Latvia) and 41 (Albania) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Moreover, in the default access list, originally 16 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path). However, since the Champions League title holders, Real Madrid, which were guaranteed a berth in the Champions League group stage, already qualified via their domestic league, only 15 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path) after the Champions League access list was rebalanced. As a result, only 16 teams entered the Champions Path second qualifying round (two of the losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were drawn to receive byes to the third qualifying round).

Scheduleedit

The schedule of the competition was as follows. Matches were scheduled for Thursdays apart from the final, which took place on a Wednesday, though exceptionally could take place on Tuesdays or Wednesdays due to scheduling conflicts (especially featuring teams from associations where there were few approved stadiums, such as Gibraltar and Wales). Scheduled kick-off times starting from the group stage were 18:45 and 21:00 CEST/CET, though exceptionally could take place at 16:30 due to geographical reasons.[11]

As the 2022 FIFA World Cup took place in Qatar between 20 November and 18 December 2022, the group stage commenced in the first week of September 2022 and concluded in the first week of November 2022 to make way for the World Cup.

The draws for the qualifying round were held at the UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.[12] The group stage draw took place in Istanbul, Turkey.[13]

The draw for the group stage was held on 26 August 2022. The 32 teams were drawn into eight groups of four. For the draw, the teams were seeded into four pots, each of eight teams, based on their 2022 UEFA club coefficients.[15] Teams from the same association and, for political reasons, teams from Serbia and Kosovo could not be drawn into the same group.

All teams besides AZ, Basel, CFR Cluj, Gent, Partizan, Slavia Prague and Slovan Bratislava, who competed in last season's group stage, made their debut appearances in the group stage. Ballkani, Djurgårdens IF, Dnipro-1, Pyunik, RFS, Silkeborg, Slovácko, Vaduz and Žalgiris made their debut appearances in a UEFA competition group stage. Ballkani, Vaduz and Žalgiris were the first teams from Kosovo, Liechtenstein and Lithuania, respectively, to play in a UEFA competition group stage.

A total of 28 national associations were represented in the group stage.

Knockout phaseedit
Main article: 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League knockout phase

In the knockout phase, teams played against each other over two legs on a home-and-away basis, except for the one-match final. The mechanism of the draws for each round was as follows:

In the draw for the knockout round play-offs, the eight group runners-up were seeded, and the eight Europa League group third-placed teams were unseeded. The seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
In the draw for the round of 16, the eight group winners were seeded, and the eight winners of the knockout round play-offs were unseeded. Again, the seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
In the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals, there were no seedings, and teams from the same association could be drawn against each other. As the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals were held together before the quarter-finals were played, the identity of the quarter-final winners was not known at the time of the semi-final draw. A draw was also held to determine which semi-final winner would be designated as the "home" team for the final (for administrative purposes as it was played at a neutral venue).

The 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League was the second season of the UEFA Europa Conference League, Europe's tertiary club football tournament organised by UEFA.

The final was played at Fortuna Arena in Prague, Czech Republic.[3] It was won by West Ham United, who defeated Fiorentina 2–1, and qualified for the 2023–24 UEFA Europa League group stage as a result.[4]

As the title holders, Roma qualified for the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League. They were unable to defend their title after advancing to the Europa League knockout phase.

Association team allocationedit

A total of 177 teams from 54 of the 55 UEFA member associations (excluding Russia) participated in the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League. The association ranking based on the UEFA country coefficients was used to determine the number of participating teams for each association:[5]

Associations 1–5 each had one team qualify.
Associations 6–17 (except Russia)[Note RUS] and 51–55 each had two teams qualify.
Associations 18–50 (except Liechtenstein)[Note LIE] each had three teams qualify.
Liechtenstein had one team qualify as they organized only a domestic cup and no domestic league.[Note LIE]
Moreover, 18 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Champions League and 25 teams eliminated from the 2022–23 UEFA Europa League were transferred to the Europa Conference League.
Association rankingedit

For the 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League, the associations were allocated places according to their 2021 UEFA country coefficients, which took into account their performance in European competitions from 2016–17 to 2020–21.[6]

Apart from the allocation based on the country coefficients, associations could have additional teams participating in the Europa Conference League, as noted below:

(UCL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Champions League
(UEL) – Additional teams transferred from the UEFA Europa League

Distributionedit

The following was the access list for this season.[7] In the default access list, the title holders of the Europa Conference League qualified for the Europa League group stage.

Due to the suspension of Russia for the 2022–23 European season, the following changes to the access list were made:

The cup winners of association 16 (Serbia) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 18 (Croatia) and 19 (Switzerland) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 30 to 39 (Poland, Slovenia, Slovakia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republic of Ireland, North Macedonia and Armenia) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Since several changes were made in the Europa League access list following the qualification of the Europa Conference League title holders to the Europa League group stage, the following changes to the access list were made:

The cup winners of association 17 (Czech Republic) enter the Europa League third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of association 20 (Greece) enter the third qualifying round instead of the second qualifying round.
The cup winners of associations 40 (Latvia) and 41 (Albania) enter the second qualifying round instead of the first qualifying round.

Moreover, in the default access list, originally 16 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path). However, since the Champions League title holders, Real Madrid, which were guaranteed a berth in the Champions League group stage, already qualified via their domestic league, only 15 losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were transferred to the Europa Conference League second qualifying round (Champions Path) after the Champions League access list was rebalanced. As a result, only 16 teams entered the Champions Path second qualifying round (two of the losers from the Champions League first qualifying round were drawn to receive byes to the third qualifying round).

Scheduleedit

The schedule of the competition was as follows. Matches were scheduled for Thursdays apart from the final, which took place on a Wednesday, though exceptionally could take place on Tuesdays or Wednesdays due to scheduling conflicts (especially featuring teams from associations where there were few approved stadiums, such as Gibraltar and Wales). Scheduled kick-off times starting from the group stage were 18:45 and 21:00 CEST/CET, though exceptionally could take place at 16:30 due to geographical reasons.[11]

As the 2022 FIFA World Cup took place in Qatar between 20 November and 18 December 2022, the group stage commenced in the first week of September 2022 and concluded in the first week of November 2022 to make way for the World Cup.

The draws for the qualifying round were held at the UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.[12] The group stage draw took place in Istanbul, Turkey.[13]

The draw for the group stage was held on 26 August 2022. The 32 teams were drawn into eight groups of four. For the draw, the teams were seeded into four pots, each of eight teams, based on their 2022 UEFA club coefficients.[15] Teams from the same association and, for political reasons, teams from Serbia and Kosovo could not be drawn into the same group.

All teams besides AZ, Basel, CFR Cluj, Gent, Partizan, Slavia Prague and Slovan Bratislava, who competed in last season's group stage, made their debut appearances in the group stage. Ballkani, Djurgårdens IF, Dnipro-1, Pyunik, RFS, Silkeborg, Slovácko, Vaduz and Žalgiris made their debut appearances in a UEFA competition group stage. Ballkani, Vaduz and Žalgiris were the first teams from Kosovo, Liechtenstein and Lithuania, respectively, to play in a UEFA competition group stage.

A total of 28 national associations were represented in the group stage.

Knockout phaseedit
Main article: 2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League knockout phase

In the knockout phase, teams played against each other over two legs on a home-and-away basis, except for the one-match final. The mechanism of the draws for each round was as follows:

In the draw for the knockout round play-offs, the eight group runners-up were seeded, and the eight Europa League group third-placed teams were unseeded. The seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
In the draw for the round of 16, the eight group winners were seeded, and the eight winners of the knockout round play-offs were unseeded. Again, the seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
In the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals, there were no seedings, and teams from the same association could be drawn against each other. As the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals were held together before the quarter-finals were played, the identity of the quarter-final winners was not known at the time of the semi-final draw. A draw was also held to determine which semi-final winner would be designated as the "home" team for the final (for administrative purposes as it was played at a neutral venue).

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League knockout phase** began on 16 February with the knockout round play-offs and ended on 7 June 2023 with the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_final "2023 UEFA Europa Conference League final") at the [Fortuna Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Arena "Fortuna Arena") in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), Czech Republic, to decide the champions of the [2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-schedule-1) A total of 24 teams competed in the knockout phase.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-regulations-2)

Times are [CET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Time "Central European Time")/[CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time"),[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-3) as listed by UEFA (local times, if different, are in parentheses).

## Qualified teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualified teams")]

The knockout phase involved 24 teams: the 16 teams which qualified as winners and runners-up of each of the eight groups in the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_group_stage "2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League group stage"), and the eight third-placed teams from the [Europa League group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage "2022–23 UEFA Europa League group stage").

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Format")]

Each tie in the [knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament"), apart from the final, was played over [two legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie"), with each team playing one leg at home. The team that scored more goals on aggregate over the two legs advanced to the next round. If the aggregate score was level, then 30 minutes of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") were played (the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was not applied). If the score was still level at the end of extra time, the winners were decided by a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"). In the final, which was played as a single match, if the score was level at the end of normal time, extra time would be played, followed by a penalty shoot-out if the score was still level.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-regulations-2) The mechanism of the draws for each round was as follows:

*   In the draw for the knockout round play-offs, the eight group runners-up were seeded, and the eight Europa League group third-placed teams were unseeded. The seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
*   In the draw for the round of 16, the eight group winners were seeded, and the eight winners of the knockout round play-offs were unseeded. Again, the seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
*   In the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals, there were no seedings, and teams from the same association could be drawn against each other. As the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals were held together before the quarter-finals were played, the identity of the quarter-final winners was not known at the time of the semi-final draw. A draw was also held to determine which semi-final winner would be designated as the "home" team for the final (for administrative purposes as it was played at a neutral venue).

In the knockout phase, teams from the same or nearby cities (Roma and Lazio, Fenerbahçe and İstanbul Başakşehir, and Anderlecht and Union SG, who share the [same stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_Vanden_Stock_Stadium "Constant Vanden Stock Stadium")), the first team listed played in the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") were not scheduled to play at home on the same day, due to logistics and crowd control. To avoid such scheduling conflicts, UEFA had to make adjustments. For the knockout round playoffs and a round of 16, since both teams were in the same pot and must play at home in a given leg, the home match of the team that was not the domestic cup or Europa Conference League winner, or lower domestic ranking (if neither is the domestic cup or Europa Conference League winner; i.e. Lazio and Anderlecht for this season), was moved from Thursday to Wednesday.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-4) For the quarter-finals and semi-finals, if the two teams were drawn to play at home for the same leg, the order of legs of the tie involving the team with the lowest priority was reversed from the original draw.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-6)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The **2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League knockout phase** began on 16 February with the knockout round play-offs and ended on 7 June 2023 with the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_final "2023 UEFA Europa Conference League final") at the [Fortuna Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Arena "Fortuna Arena") in [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague"), Czech Republic, to decide the champions of the [2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-schedule-1) A total of 24 teams competed in the knockout phase.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-regulations-2)

Times are [CET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Time "Central European Time")/[CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time"),[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-3) as listed by UEFA (local times, if different, are in parentheses).

## Qualified teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Qualified teams")]

The knockout phase involved 24 teams: the 16 teams which qualified as winners and runners-up of each of the eight groups in the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_group_stage "2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League group stage"), and the eight third-placed teams from the [Europa League group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League_group_stage "2022–23 UEFA Europa League group stage").

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Format")]

Each tie in the [knockout phase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament"), apart from the final, was played over [two legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie"), with each team playing one leg at home. The team that scored more goals on aggregate over the two legs advanced to the next round. If the aggregate score was level, then 30 minutes of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") were played (the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was not applied). If the score was still level at the end of extra time, the winners were decided by a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"). In the final, which was played as a single match, if the score was level at the end of normal time, extra time would be played, followed by a penalty shoot-out if the score was still level.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-regulations-2) The mechanism of the draws for each round was as follows:

*   In the draw for the knockout round play-offs, the eight group runners-up were seeded, and the eight Europa League group third-placed teams were unseeded. The seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
*   In the draw for the round of 16, the eight group winners were seeded, and the eight winners of the knockout round play-offs were unseeded. Again, the seeded teams were drawn against the unseeded teams, with the seeded teams hosting the second leg. Teams from the same association could not be drawn against each other.
*   In the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals, there were no seedings, and teams from the same association could be drawn against each other. As the draws for the quarter-finals and semi-finals were held together before the quarter-finals were played, the identity of the quarter-final winners was not known at the time of the semi-final draw. A draw was also held to determine which semi-final winner would be designated as the "home" team for the final (for administrative purposes as it was played at a neutral venue).

In the knockout phase, teams from the same or nearby cities (Roma and Lazio, Fenerbahçe and İstanbul Başakşehir, and Anderlecht and Union SG, who share the [same stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constant_Vanden_Stock_Stadium "Constant Vanden Stock Stadium")), the first team listed played in the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") were not scheduled to play at home on the same day, due to logistics and crowd control. To avoid such scheduling conflicts, UEFA had to make adjustments. For the knockout round playoffs and a round of 16, since both teams were in the same pot and must play at home in a given leg, the home match of the team that was not the domestic cup or Europa Conference League winner, or lower domestic ranking (if neither is the domestic cup or Europa Conference League winner; i.e. Lazio and Anderlecht for this season), was moved from Thursday to Wednesday.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-4) For the quarter-finals and semi-finals, if the two teams were drawn to play at home for the same leg, the order of legs of the tie involving the team with the lowest priority was reversed from the original draw.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League_knockout_phase#cite_note-6)

The **2022–23 Eredivisie** was the 67th season of the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie"), the premier football competition in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 28 May 2023. As the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") started on 20 November, the last round before stoppage was held on 12–13 November. The league resumed games on 6 January.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-:0-1)

[Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") became the champions in round 32, beating [Go Ahead Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Ahead_Eagles "Go Ahead Eagles") 3–0 at [De Kuip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam") on 14 May 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-2)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

[Emmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Emmen "FC Emmen") (promoted after a one-year absence), [Volendam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volendam "FC Volendam") (promoted after a thirteen-year absence) and [Excelsior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Rotterdam "Excelsior Rotterdam") (promoted after a three-year absence) were promoted from the [2021–22 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Eerste_Divisie "2021–22 Eerste Divisie"). The **2022–23 Eredivisie** was the 67th season of the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie"), the premier football competition in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"). It began on 5 August 2022 and concluded on 28 May 2023. As the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") started on 20 November, the last round before stoppage was held on 12–13 November. The league resumed games on 6 January.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-:0-1)

[Feyenoord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feyenoord "Feyenoord") became the champions in round 32, beating [Go Ahead Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_Ahead_Eagles "Go Ahead Eagles") 3–0 at [De Kuip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Kuip "De Kuip") in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam") on 14 May 2023.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie#cite_note-2)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Teams")]

[Emmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Emmen "FC Emmen") (promoted after a one-year absence), [Volendam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Volendam "FC Volendam") (promoted after a thirteen-year absence) and [Excelsior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excelsior_Rotterdam "Excelsior Rotterdam") (promoted after a three-year absence) were promoted from the [2021–22 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Eerste_Divisie "2021–22 Eerste Divisie"). [Willem II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_II_(football_club) "Willem II (football club)") (relegated after eight years in the top flight), [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") (relegated after ten years in the top flight), and [Heracles Almelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heracles_Almelo "Heracles Almelo") (relegated after seventeen years in the top flight) were relegated to the [2022–23 Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eerste_Divisie "2022–23 Eerste Divisie").

The **2022–23 season** was the 56th in the history of [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") and their 25th consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie "2022–23 Eredivisie"), the [KNVB Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_KNVB_Cup "2022–23 KNVB Cup"), and the UEFA Europa Conference League.

The **2022–23 season** was the 56th in the history of [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") and their 25th consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Eredivisie "2022–23 Eredivisie"), the [KNVB Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_KNVB_Cup "2022–23 KNVB Cup"), and the UEFA Europa Conference League.

The **2022–23 Swiss Super League** (referred to as the **Credit Suisse Super League** for sponsoring reasons) was the 126th season of [top-tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Super_League "Swiss Super League") competitive [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") in [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") and the 20th under its current name and format. With this season, the Swiss Super League became the [longest continuously running top-flight national league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_football_competitions "List of oldest football competitions").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched1-2)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

A total of ten teams are competing in the league: nine teams of the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Swiss_Super_League "2021–22 Swiss Super League") will participate in the league again. [FC Lausanne-Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lausanne-Sport "FC Lausanne-Sport"), who came in last place, were relegated and are replaced by the [2021–22 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Swiss_Challenge_League "2021–22 Swiss Challenge League") champions [Winterthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Winterthur "FC Winterthur"). [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") remains in the league as the winner of the Relegation/Promotion playoff. [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich "FC Zürich") are the defending champions.

After Swiss teams gained 7.75 points in European championships in the 2021–22 season, the [Swiss Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Football_Association "Swiss Football Association") jumped five spots in the [UEFA association ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient") to rank 14, granting them five spots in European championships in the 2023–24 season. This means that first and second ranked teams of the 2022–23 season will participate in the [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League#Third_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") and [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League#Second_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") rounds of the [2023–24 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") qualification, respectively, while the third and fourth enter the [second round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#Second_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League") of the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League") qualification. Furthermore, the champion of the [2022-23 Swiss Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022-23_Swiss_Cup "2022-23 Swiss Cup") enters the [third qualification round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League#Third_qualifying_round "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") for the [2023–24 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-uefa-3)

Due to the format change and the increased number of teams starting with the [2023–24 Swiss Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Swiss_Super_League "2023–24 Swiss Super League"), this season will function as a transition season. As a result, no teams will be directly relegated to the [2023–24 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Challenge_League "Swiss Challenge League"). Instead the last-placed team will play a relegation playoff against the third team of the [2022–23 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Challenge_League "2022–23 Swiss Challenge League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-newmode-4)

### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The playing schedule of the season, as well as dates and times for the first nine matchdays were announced on 17 June 2022.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched1-2) The first matchday would be held on the weekend of 16 and 17 July 2022. However, the first round match [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") – [Grasshoppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasshopper_Club_Z%C3%BCrich "Grasshopper Club Zürich") is postponed until 10 August 2022, due to lack of venues. The match [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") – [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel"), originally scheduled for 31 July 2022 (Matchday 3), is also postponed to 9 November 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched2-5) Furthermore, scheduled dates for champion [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich "FC Zürich") for matchdays 4, 5, and 8 may be swapped subject to their [Champions League qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League_qualifying_phase_and_play-off_round "2022–23 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round") schedule.

The exact schedule for matchdays 10 through 18 were announced on 2 September 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched2-5) Due to the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), which will be held in November and December 2022, the league will go on a two-month break, after matchday 16 on 13 November 2022. The winter break will thus occur two rounds earlier than usual, with matchdays 17 and 18 to be held in January 2023. On 22 November 2022, fixtures of matchdays 19 through 27 were scheduled.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched3-6) Matchdays 28 through 36 were scheduled on 15 March 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched4-7)

The last matchday will be on 29 May 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched4-7) Following the end of the season, the two legs of the Relegation Play-off will be played on 3 and 6 June 2023, respectively.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-rel-8)

## Relegation play-off

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Relegation play-off")]

The relegation play-off will be played in a two-legged game between the last place team of the Super League and the third placed team of the [Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Challenge_League "2022–23 Swiss Challenge League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-newmode-4) The first leg will be held on 3 June 2023, with the representative of the Super League hosting.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-rel-8) The second leg will be held on 6 June 2023. Winner of the play-off is whichever teams scores most in both games (no [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule")).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-36) In case of a tie at the end of the two games, 30 minutes of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") (two times 15 minutes) are added, followed by a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"), in case the teams are still tied.

The **2022–23 Swiss Super League** (referred to as the **Credit Suisse Super League** for sponsoring reasons) was the 126th season of [top-tier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Super_League "Swiss Super League") competitive [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") in [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") and the 20th under its current name and format. With this season, the Swiss Super League became the [longest continuously running top-flight national league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_football_competitions "List of oldest football competitions").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched1-2)

## Overview

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Overview")]

A total of ten teams are competing in the league: nine teams of the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Swiss_Super_League "2021–22 Swiss Super League") will participate in the league again. [FC Lausanne-Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Lausanne-Sport "FC Lausanne-Sport"), who came in last place, were relegated and are replaced by the [2021–22 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Swiss_Challenge_League "2021–22 Swiss Challenge League") champions [Winterthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Winterthur "FC Winterthur"). [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") remains in the league as the winner of the Relegation/Promotion playoff. [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich "FC Zürich") are the defending champions.

After Swiss teams gained 7.75 points in European championships in the 2021–22 season, the [Swiss Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Football_Association "Swiss Football Association") jumped five spots in the [UEFA association ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_coefficient#Men's_Association_coefficient "UEFA coefficient") to rank 14, granting them five spots in European championships in the 2023–24 season. This means that first and second ranked teams of the 2022–23 season will participate in the [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League#Third_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") and [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League#Second_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") rounds of the [2023–24 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") qualification, respectively, while the third and fourth enter the [second round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League#Second_qualifying_round "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League") of the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League") qualification. Furthermore, the champion of the [2022-23 Swiss Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022-23_Swiss_Cup "2022-23 Swiss Cup") enters the [third qualification round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League#Third_qualifying_round "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") for the [2023–24 UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-uefa-3)

Due to the format change and the increased number of teams starting with the [2023–24 Swiss Super League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Swiss_Super_League "2023–24 Swiss Super League"), this season will function as a transition season. As a result, no teams will be directly relegated to the [2023–24 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Challenge_League "Swiss Challenge League"). Instead the last-placed team will play a relegation playoff against the third team of the [2022–23 Swiss Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Challenge_League "2022–23 Swiss Challenge League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-newmode-4)

### Schedule

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Schedule")]

The playing schedule of the season, as well as dates and times for the first nine matchdays were announced on 17 June 2022.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched1-2) The first matchday would be held on the weekend of 16 and 17 July 2022. However, the first round match [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") – [Grasshoppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasshopper_Club_Z%C3%BCrich "Grasshopper Club Zürich") is postponed until 10 August 2022, due to lack of venues. The match [Luzern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Luzern "FC Luzern") – [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Basel "FC Basel"), originally scheduled for 31 July 2022 (Matchday 3), is also postponed to 9 November 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched2-5) Furthermore, scheduled dates for champion [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Z%C3%BCrich "FC Zürich") for matchdays 4, 5, and 8 may be swapped subject to their [Champions League qualifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League_qualifying_phase_and_play-off_round "2022–23 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round") schedule.

The exact schedule for matchdays 10 through 18 were announced on 2 September 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched2-5) Due to the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), which will be held in November and December 2022, the league will go on a two-month break, after matchday 16 on 13 November 2022. The winter break will thus occur two rounds earlier than usual, with matchdays 17 and 18 to be held in January 2023. On 22 November 2022, fixtures of matchdays 19 through 27 were scheduled.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched3-6) Matchdays 28 through 36 were scheduled on 15 March 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched4-7)

The last matchday will be on 29 May 2023.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-sched4-7) Following the end of the season, the two legs of the Relegation Play-off will be played on 3 and 6 June 2023, respectively.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-rel-8)

## Relegation play-off

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Relegation play-off")]

The relegation play-off will be played in a two-legged game between the last place team of the Super League and the third placed team of the [Challenge League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Challenge_League "2022–23 Swiss Challenge League").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-newmode-4) The first leg will be held on 3 June 2023, with the representative of the Super League hosting.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-rel-8) The second leg will be held on 6 June 2023. Winner of the play-off is whichever teams scores most in both games (no [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule")).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Swiss_Super_League#cite_note-36) In case of a tie at the end of the two games, 30 minutes of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") (two times 15 minutes) are added, followed by a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)"), in case the teams are still tied.

The **2022–23 Premier League** was the 31st season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") and the 124th season of top-flight English football overall. [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C.") were the three promoted clubs from the [2021–22 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_EFL_Championship "2021–22 EFL Championship"), replacing [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.").

Following [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.")'s defeat to Nottingham Forest on 20 May, [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") officially secured a [third consecutive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-peat "Three-peat") Premier League title with three games to spare, becoming the second club after local rivals [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") to achieve the feat in the Premier League era. It was their ninth English title overall and their seventh since 1992.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-1) The league title was the first leg in a [treble-winning season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)") for City, as they would later go on to win the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_FA_Cup "2022–23 FA Cup") and [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League "2022–23 UEFA Champions League"), a feat which only United had previously achieved in England. Meanwhile, Arsenal broke the record of spending the greatest number of days, with 248, on top of the league in a top flight season without winning the title in English top flight history.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

This season was also the first since [2017–18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Premier_League "2017–18 Premier League"), and only the fourth Premier League season overall, where all three promoted teams at the start of the season avoided relegation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-3) This was also the first time since [2014–15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League "2014–15 Premier League") that the team 20th at Christmas ([Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022-23_Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C._season "2022-23 Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. season")), managed to avoid relegation.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

The 2022–23 season was the highest-scoring 38-game season in Premier League history, with 1,084 goals scored and a 2.85 goals per match ratio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland") broke the Premier League record for most goals scored by a player in one season with 36 goals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

It was also the second Premier League season in a row where over 15 millions fans attended matches and with total of 15,289,340 spectators a new competition record was set.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

The season began with Arsenal going on a five-game unbeaten streak before they played [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") where they lost 3–1.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-8)[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") got off to a strong start, having signed striker [Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland"); they went on a nine-game unbeaten run before losing at [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in October. Arsenal were top of the table for much of the season, at one point holding an eight point lead over Manchester City. However, a run of three consecutive draws allowed City to cut their lead, ultimately taking control after beating them 4–1 at the [Etihad Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium"). Two consecutive losses against [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.") and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C.") left Arsenal four points behind Manchester City with three more games to play, with the latter result confirming City as champions.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-9) They were presented with the Premier League trophy on 21 May 2023.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

Manchester United returned to the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") in [Erik ten Hag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_ten_Hag "Erik ten Hag")'s debut season as the club's manager, in addition to winning the [Carabao Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_EFL_Cup "2022–23 EFL Cup") – their first trophy since [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Manchester_United_F.C._season "2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season") – and reaching the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_FA_Cup_final "2023 FA Cup final") of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_FA_Cup "2022–23 FA Cup"). [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") qualified for the Champions League for the first time in [20 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_Newcastle_United_F.C._season "2002–03 Newcastle United F.C. season"), their highest finish since [Sir Bobby Robson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Robson "Bobby Robson") was the club's manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-11) Liverpool endured a difficult season and finished 5th, missing out on Champions League football for the first time since [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Liverpool_F.C._season "2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season"). Notably, they thrashed [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth")[9–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._9%E2%80%930_AFC_Bournemouth "Liverpool F.C. 9–0 AFC Bournemouth") and rivals Manchester United 7–0.

Despite spending over £600m on new transfers under new ownership led by [Todd Boehly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Boehly "Todd Boehly"), [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") had one of their worst Premier League seasons to date, with the Blues finishing in the bottom half of the table after first sacking [Thomas Tuchel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Tuchel "Thomas Tuchel") in September, and then sacking his successor [Graham Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Potter "Graham Potter") the following April, after only seven months in charge. [Frank Lampard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lampard "Frank Lampard") returned to the club as interim manager, having previously been sacked himself in January 2021, but the team fared no better under his stewardship either. They ended up finishing 12th, their lowest league finish since [1993–94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_Chelsea_F.C._season "1993–94 Chelsea F.C. season"), and had accumulated just 44 points – their lowest ever in a Premier League season.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-12)

Brighton & Hove Albion lost manager Potter to Chelsea in September, but his successor [Roberto De Zerbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_De_Zerbi "Roberto De Zerbi") led the team to a club record finish of 6th, and qualified for the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League"), the first European qualification in the history of the club.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-MacInnes_2023-13)

[Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C.") secured qualification for European football for the first time since [2009–10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Aston_Villa_F.C._season "2009–10 Aston Villa F.C. season"); an indifferent start to the season saw the departure of manager [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard"), but his successor [Unai Emery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unai_Emery "Unai Emery"), along with in-form striker [Ollie Watkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollie_Watkins "Ollie Watkins"), saw Villa climb the table in the second half of the season to finish 7th and qualify for the [Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-14)[Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") had an erratic season, with manager [Antonio Conte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Conte "Antonio Conte") departing by mutual consent in March, days after publicly criticising the team in a post-match press conference.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-15) He was initially replaced by his assistant [Cristian Stellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristian_Stellini "Cristian Stellini") until the end of the season, but a poor run, culminating in a 6–1 defeat away to Newcastle, where the team were 5–0 down after just 20 minutes, saw him sacked and replaced by [Ryan Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Mason "Ryan Mason") as caretaker manager. Tottenham ended up finishing 8th, failing to qualify for European football for the first time since [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season"), and finishing below rivals Arsenal in the league for the first time since [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2015–16 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season").

[Brentford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentford_F.C. "Brentford F.C.") enjoyed one of the best seasons in their history, at one point going on a 12-match unbeaten run. They notably thrashed Manchester United 4–0 and beat Liverpool 3–1, and were the only team to beat Manchester City twice. Their 9th-place finish marked their highest finish in top-flight football since 1938.

Bournemouth, who were tipped for relegation at the start of the season (particularly after their 9–0 loss to Liverpool at [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield"), which saw manager [Scott Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Parker "Scott Parker") sacked soon after),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-16) defied the critics by avoiding relegation, with [Gary O'Neil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_O'Neil "Gary O'Neil"), first as interim, then permanent manager, guiding the team to safety. Nottingham Forest broke the record for most signings in a Premier League season with 21,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-17) and a late run of home victories over Brighton, [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and Arsenal secured safety. The final newly promoted side, [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), enjoyed a successful return to the top flight with a 10th place finish.

Southampton were the first team to be relegated after eleven consecutive years in the top flight. The Saints sacked [Ralph Hasenhüttl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Hasenh%C3%BCttl "Ralph Hasenhüttl") in November after just under four years in charge and [Nathan Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Jones_(Welsh_footballer) "Nathan Jones (Welsh footballer)") was appointed as his successor. He would then be dismissed in February after winning just once in his eight league matches in charge. He was replaced for the rest of the season by [Rubén Sellés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Sell%C3%A9s "Rubén Sellés"), who was unable to turn the dire situation around, and a 2–0 home loss to Fulham on 13 May sealed their fate, as they finished at the bottom of the table.

Going into the final day of the season, two relegation places were still to be confirmed, with [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") and [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") all potentially at threat of relegation. Leeds failed to repeat their last day escape of the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Premier_League "2021–22 Premier League") and were also relegated after three years back in the top flight, losing 4–1 at home to Tottenham Hotspur. Everton escaped relegation after a 1–0 win over Bournemouth, extending their top flight stay to a 70th consecutive year.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-19) The Toffees' survival confirmed Leicester's relegation after a nine year stay in the top flight, despite a 2–1 home win over [West Ham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Their relegation came only [seven years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League "2015–16 Premier League") after being crowned champions of England, and they became only the second club in the Premier League era after [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") to be relegated as previous title winners.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-20)

### Developments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Developments")]

Starting from the 2022–23 season, clubs are able to make five [substitutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") rather than three. These substitutions can be made in three stoppages during game time, and additionally at half time,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-21) in line with other top European leagues – [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A"), [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") and the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

There was a mid-season break for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") in Qatar, with the last matches before the hiatus played on the weekend of 12–13 November 2022 and the first matches after the World Cup played on 26 December 2022, after the [World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2022 FIFA World Cup final") on 18 December 2022.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-22)

On 9 September 2022, all Premier League matches scheduled for 10–12 September were postponed as a mark of respect due to the [death of Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Elizabeth_II "Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-Premier_League_statement-23) The following week, three Premier League matches scheduled for 17–18 September were postponed due to the policing issues surrounding Queen Elizabeth II's state funeral on 19 September.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-Premier_League_statement-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-25) Also, in the same week, the Arsenal game against Manchester City, scheduled for 19 October, was postponed to accommodate Arsenal's [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") tie with [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven"), which was itself postponed from 15 September to 20 October.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-28)

The promoted teams were [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth"), and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C."), who returned to the top flight after respective absences of one, two and twenty-three years. They replaced [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") (relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_EFL_Championship "2022–23 EFL Championship") after a six-year top flight spell), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C."), and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") (both teams relegated after just one year back in the top flight).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
