The **2022–23 Premier League** was the 31st season of the [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") and the 124th season of top-flight English football overall. [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth") and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C.") were the three promoted clubs from the [2021–22 EFL Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_EFL_Championship "2021–22 EFL Championship"), replacing [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C."), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C.") and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.").

Following [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.")'s defeat to Nottingham Forest on 20 May, [Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") officially secured a [third consecutive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-peat "Three-peat") Premier League title with three games to spare, becoming the second club after local rivals [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") to achieve the feat in the Premier League era. It was their ninth English title overall and their seventh since 1992.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-1) The league title was the first leg in a [treble-winning season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_(association_football)#Continental_trebles "Treble (association football)") for City, as they would later go on to win the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_FA_Cup "2022–23 FA Cup") and [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Champions_League "2022–23 UEFA Champions League"), a feat which only United had previously achieved in England. Meanwhile, Arsenal broke the record of spending the greatest number of days, with 248, on top of the league in a top flight season without winning the title in English top flight history.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-2)

This season was also the first since [2017–18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Premier_League "2017–18 Premier League"), and only the fourth Premier League season overall, where all three promoted teams at the start of the season avoided relegation.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-3) This was also the first time since [2014–15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Premier_League "2014–15 Premier League") that the team 20th at Christmas ([Wolverhampton Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022-23_Wolverhampton_Wanderers_F.C._season "2022-23 Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. season")), managed to avoid relegation.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-4)

The 2022–23 season was the highest-scoring 38-game season in Premier League history, with 1,084 goals scored and a 2.85 goals per match ratio.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-5)[Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland") broke the Premier League record for most goals scored by a player in one season with 36 goals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-6)

It was also the second Premier League season in a row where over 15 millions fans attended matches and with total of 15,289,340 spectators a new competition record was set.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-7)

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

The season began with Arsenal going on a five-game unbeaten streak before they played [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") at [Old Trafford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford") where they lost 3–1.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-8)[Manchester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") got off to a strong start, having signed striker [Erling Haaland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erling_Haaland "Erling Haaland"); they went on a nine-game unbeaten run before losing at [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") in October. Arsenal were top of the table for much of the season, at one point holding an eight point lead over Manchester City. However, a run of three consecutive draws allowed City to cut their lead, ultimately taking control after beating them 4–1 at the [Etihad Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Manchester_Stadium "City of Manchester Stadium"). Two consecutive losses against [Brighton & Hove Albion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brighton_&_Hove_Albion_F.C. "Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.") and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C.") left Arsenal four points behind Manchester City with three more games to play, with the latter result confirming City as champions.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-9) They were presented with the Premier League trophy on 21 May 2023.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-10)

Manchester United returned to the [Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League") in [Erik ten Hag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_ten_Hag "Erik ten Hag")'s debut season as the club's manager, in addition to winning the [Carabao Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_EFL_Cup "2022–23 EFL Cup") – their first trophy since [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Manchester_United_F.C._season "2016–17 Manchester United F.C. season") – and reaching the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_FA_Cup_final "2023 FA Cup final") of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_FA_Cup "2022–23 FA Cup"). [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.") qualified for the Champions League for the first time in [20 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002%E2%80%9303_Newcastle_United_F.C._season "2002–03 Newcastle United F.C. season"), their highest finish since [Sir Bobby Robson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Robson "Bobby Robson") was the club's manager.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-11) Liverpool endured a difficult season and finished 5th, missing out on Champions League football for the first time since [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Liverpool_F.C._season "2015–16 Liverpool F.C. season"). Notably, they thrashed [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth")[9–0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._9%E2%80%930_AFC_Bournemouth "Liverpool F.C. 9–0 AFC Bournemouth") and rivals Manchester United 7–0.

Despite spending over £600m on new transfers under new ownership led by [Todd Boehly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Boehly "Todd Boehly"), [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") had one of their worst Premier League seasons to date, with the Blues finishing in the bottom half of the table after first sacking [Thomas Tuchel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Tuchel "Thomas Tuchel") in September, and then sacking his successor [Graham Potter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Potter "Graham Potter") the following April, after only seven months in charge. [Frank Lampard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lampard "Frank Lampard") returned to the club as interim manager, having previously been sacked himself in January 2021, but the team fared no better under his stewardship either. They ended up finishing 12th, their lowest league finish since [1993–94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993%E2%80%9394_Chelsea_F.C._season "1993–94 Chelsea F.C. season"), and had accumulated just 44 points – their lowest ever in a Premier League season.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-12)

Brighton & Hove Albion lost manager Potter to Chelsea in September, but his successor [Roberto De Zerbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_De_Zerbi "Roberto De Zerbi") led the team to a club record finish of 6th, and qualified for the [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa League"), the first European qualification in the history of the club.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-MacInnes_2023-13)

[Aston Villa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aston_Villa_F.C. "Aston Villa F.C.") secured qualification for European football for the first time since [2009–10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Aston_Villa_F.C._season "2009–10 Aston Villa F.C. season"); an indifferent start to the season saw the departure of manager [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard"), but his successor [Unai Emery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unai_Emery "Unai Emery"), along with in-form striker [Ollie Watkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollie_Watkins "Ollie Watkins"), saw Villa climb the table in the second half of the season to finish 7th and qualify for the [Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-14)[Tottenham Hotspur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C. "Tottenham Hotspur F.C.") had an erratic season, with manager [Antonio Conte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Conte "Antonio Conte") departing by mutual consent in March, days after publicly criticising the team in a post-match press conference.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-15) He was initially replaced by his assistant [Cristian Stellini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristian_Stellini "Cristian Stellini") until the end of the season, but a poor run, culminating in a 6–1 defeat away to Newcastle, where the team were 5–0 down after just 20 minutes, saw him sacked and replaced by [Ryan Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Mason "Ryan Mason") as caretaker manager. Tottenham ended up finishing 8th, failing to qualify for European football for the first time since [2008–09](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season"), and finishing below rivals Arsenal in the league for the first time since [2015–16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Tottenham_Hotspur_F.C._season "2015–16 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season").

[Brentford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentford_F.C. "Brentford F.C.") enjoyed one of the best seasons in their history, at one point going on a 12-match unbeaten run. They notably thrashed Manchester United 4–0 and beat Liverpool 3–1, and were the only team to beat Manchester City twice. Their 9th-place finish marked their highest finish in top-flight football since 1938.

Bournemouth, who were tipped for relegation at the start of the season (particularly after their 9–0 loss to Liverpool at [Anfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anfield "Anfield"), which saw manager [Scott Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Parker "Scott Parker") sacked soon after),[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-16) defied the critics by avoiding relegation, with [Gary O'Neil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_O'Neil "Gary O'Neil"), first as interim, then permanent manager, guiding the team to safety. Nottingham Forest broke the record for most signings in a Premier League season with 21,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-17) and a late run of home victories over Brighton, [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") and Arsenal secured safety. The final newly promoted side, [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), enjoyed a successful return to the top flight with a 10th place finish.

Southampton were the first team to be relegated after eleven consecutive years in the top flight. The Saints sacked [Ralph Hasenhüttl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Hasenh%C3%BCttl "Ralph Hasenhüttl") in November after just under four years in charge and [Nathan Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Jones_(Welsh_footballer) "Nathan Jones (Welsh footballer)") was appointed as his successor. He would then be dismissed in February after winning just once in his eight league matches in charge. He was replaced for the rest of the season by [Rubén Sellés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Sell%C3%A9s "Rubén Sellés"), who was unable to turn the dire situation around, and a 2–0 home loss to Fulham on 13 May sealed their fate, as they finished at the bottom of the table.

Going into the final day of the season, two relegation places were still to be confirmed, with [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C."), [Leeds United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_United_F.C. "Leeds United F.C.") and [Leicester City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester_City_F.C. "Leicester City F.C.") all potentially at threat of relegation. Leeds failed to repeat their last day escape of the [previous season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Premier_League "2021–22 Premier League") and were also relegated after three years back in the top flight, losing 4–1 at home to Tottenham Hotspur. Everton escaped relegation after a 1–0 win over Bournemouth, extending their top flight stay to a 70th consecutive year.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-19) The Toffees' survival confirmed Leicester's relegation after a nine year stay in the top flight, despite a 2–1 home win over [West Ham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C."). Their relegation came only [seven years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Premier_League "2015–16 Premier League") after being crowned champions of England, and they became only the second club in the Premier League era after [Blackburn Rovers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Rovers_F.C. "Blackburn Rovers F.C.") to be relegated as previous title winners.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-20)

### Developments

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Developments")]

Starting from the 2022–23 season, clubs are able to make five [substitutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_(association_football) "Substitute (association football)") rather than three. These substitutions can be made in three stoppages during game time, and additionally at half time,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-21) in line with other top European leagues – [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A"), [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") and the [Bundesliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

There was a mid-season break for the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") in Qatar, with the last matches before the hiatus played on the weekend of 12–13 November 2022 and the first matches after the World Cup played on 26 December 2022, after the [World Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_final "2022 FIFA World Cup final") on 18 December 2022.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-22)

On 9 September 2022, all Premier League matches scheduled for 10–12 September were postponed as a mark of respect due to the [death of Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Elizabeth_II "Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-Premier_League_statement-23) The following week, three Premier League matches scheduled for 17–18 September were postponed due to the policing issues surrounding Queen Elizabeth II's state funeral on 19 September.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-Premier_League_statement-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-25) Also, in the same week, the Arsenal game against Manchester City, scheduled for 19 October, was postponed to accommodate Arsenal's [Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_UEFA_Europa_League "2022–23 UEFA Europa League") tie with [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven"), which was itself postponed from 15 September to 20 October.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League#cite_note-28)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Premier_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Teams")]

Twenty teams competed in the league – the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_EFL_Championship "2021–22 EFL Championship"). The promoted teams were [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."), [Bournemouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth"), and [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C."), who returned to the top flight after respective absences of one, two and twenty-three years. They replaced [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") (relegated to the [Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_EFL_Championship "2022–23 EFL Championship") after a six-year top flight spell), [Watford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_F.C. "Watford F.C."), and [Norwich City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwich_City_F.C. "Norwich City F.C.") (both teams relegated after just one year back in the top flight).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

# AZ move closer to their own transfer record and suddenly have their desired reinforcement in place

[Transfers](https://www.goal.com/en/category/transfers/1/k94w8e1yy9ch14mllpf4srnks)

[AZ Alkmaar](https://www.goal.com/en/team/az-alkmaar/3kfktv64h7kg7zryax1wktr5r)

****AZ have signed a new midfielder. The Alkmaar club are paying seven million euros to FC Midtjylland for the services of Valdemar Byskov, according to the Danish outlet Bold.****

Valdemar Byskov is a 21-year-old central midfielder who came through Midtjylland's youth academy and has played youth internationals for Denmark Under-21s.



Already, Byskov has made more than 100 appearances for the Danish club's first team. He has scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists.

After the weekend, Byskov will travel to the Netherlands to undergo a medical. He will then sign a long-term contract at the AFAS Stadion.

[Europa League ![Image 26: Sunderland crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/hRMDFkwiIhvjfGNfMkNk_.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) Sunderland SUN 16 Sept 2026 12:00 ![Image 27: AZ Alkmaar crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/X963ylMA_nSxn3F6AOvrP.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) AZ Alkmaar AZ](https://www.goal.com/en/match/sunderland-vs-az-alkmaar/WlL41_PTybnOP6WCtbpwW)

According to Bold, AZ are paying 'around seven million euros' for the talented playmaker. That makes Byskov one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

Still, the most expensive signing remains Weslley Patati. AZ signed him from Maccabi Tel Aviv last summer for 7.3 million euros.

# AZ move closer to their own transfer record and suddenly have their desired reinforcement in place

[Transfers](https://www.goal.com/en/category/transfers/1/k94w8e1yy9ch14mllpf4srnks)

[AZ Alkmaar](https://www.goal.com/en/team/az-alkmaar/3kfktv64h7kg7zryax1wktr5r)

****AZ have signed a new midfielder. The Alkmaar club are paying seven million euros to FC Midtjylland for the services of Valdemar Byskov, according to the Danish outlet Bold.****

Valdemar Byskov is a 21-year-old central midfielder who came through Midtjylland's youth academy and has played youth internationals for Denmark Under-21s.



Already, Byskov has made more than 100 appearances for the Danish club's first team. He has scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists.

After the weekend, Byskov will travel to the Netherlands to undergo a medical. He will then sign a long-term contract at the AFAS Stadion.

[Europa League ![Image 26: Sunderland crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/hRMDFkwiIhvjfGNfMkNk_.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) Sunderland SUN 16 Sept 2026 12:00 ![Image 27: AZ Alkmaar crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/X963ylMA_nSxn3F6AOvrP.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) AZ Alkmaar AZ](https://www.goal.com/en/match/sunderland-vs-az-alkmaar/WlL41_PTybnOP6WCtbpwW)

According to Bold, AZ are paying 'around seven million euros' for the talented playmaker. That makes Byskov one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

Still, the most expensive signing remains Weslley Patati. AZ signed him from Maccabi Tel Aviv last summer for 7.3 million euros.

# Aron Johannsson signs new contract with AZ Alkmaar

Aron Johannsson’s incredible year continues.

by[Ryan Rosenblatt](https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/authors/ryan-rosenblatt)

May 30, 2014, 5:42 PM UTC

*    

![Image 8](https://platform.starsandstripesfc.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/151/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/14732951/475348177.0.1503996945.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C5.76199955762%2C100%2C88.47600088476&w=2400)

![Image 9](https://platform.starsandstripesfc.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/151/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/14732951/475348177.0.1503996945.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C5.76199955762%2C100%2C88.47600088476&w=2400)

Dean Mouhtaropoulos

Aron Johannsson will be at AZ Alkmaar for a little while longer, or at least another team will have to pay a pretty penny to sign him from the Dutch club. The American forward has signed a new contract with the club that runs through 2018, a nice reward for his 26-goal season at AZ.

## [Fans come for the America. Will they stay? ### Ryan Rosenblatt The World Cup is proving to be a breeding ground for U.S. fans ... again.](http://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/5/28/5756476/usmnt-azerbaijan-world-cup-2014)

#### ![Image 12](http://cdn2.sbnation.com/assets/3608771/star.png) Must Reads ![Image 13](http://cdn2.sbnation.com/assets/3608771/star.png)

[Fans come for the America. Will they stay?](http://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/5/28/5756476/usmnt-azerbaijan-world-cup-2014)

Johannsson was signed by AZ just 18 months ago and after spending the first half of a season behind Jozy Altidore on the depth chart, took over the starting spot when Altidore was sold to Sunderland. It didn’t take him long to adjust to being the leading man, finishing third in the Eredisivie in goals as AZ finished eighth.

Now, Marco van Basten is the AZ manager, which should be a boon for Johannsson. The Ajax and AC Milan legend was an incredible striker and has been praised for his abilities to work with forwards, even if his ability as a manager have been questioned.

With a new contract, Johannsson can either stay at AZ long term or, more likely, move to a bigger club for a hefty fee soon. With Johannsson under contract, AZ can demand a bigger transfer fee from whoever comes calling, be it one of the Eredivisie’s biggest clubs of one from another country. If the 23-year-old continues scoring, and especially if he stars for the U.S., teams will definitely come calling and Johannsson could find himself on a much bigger stage before long.

# Aron Johannsson signs new contract with AZ Alkmaar

Aron Johannsson’s incredible year continues.

by[Ryan Rosenblatt](https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/authors/ryan-rosenblatt)

May 30, 2014, 5:42 PM UTC

*    

![Image 8](https://platform.starsandstripesfc.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/151/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/14732951/475348177.0.1503996945.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C5.76199955762%2C100%2C88.47600088476&w=2400)

![Image 9](https://platform.starsandstripesfc.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/151/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/14732951/475348177.0.1503996945.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C5.76199955762%2C100%2C88.47600088476&w=2400)

Dean Mouhtaropoulos

Aron Johannsson will be at AZ Alkmaar for a little while longer, or at least another team will have to pay a pretty penny to sign him from the Dutch club. The American forward has signed a new contract with the club that runs through 2018, a nice reward for his 26-goal season at AZ.

## [Fans come for the America. Will they stay? ### Ryan Rosenblatt The World Cup is proving to be a breeding ground for U.S. fans ... again.](http://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/5/28/5756476/usmnt-azerbaijan-world-cup-2014)

#### ![Image 12](http://cdn2.sbnation.com/assets/3608771/star.png) Must Reads ![Image 13](http://cdn2.sbnation.com/assets/3608771/star.png)

[Fans come for the America. Will they stay?](http://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/5/28/5756476/usmnt-azerbaijan-world-cup-2014)

Johannsson was signed by AZ just 18 months ago and after spending the first half of a season behind Jozy Altidore on the depth chart, took over the starting spot when Altidore was sold to Sunderland. It didn’t take him long to adjust to being the leading man, finishing third in the Eredisivie in goals as AZ finished eighth.

Now, Marco van Basten is the AZ manager, which should be a boon for Johannsson. The Ajax and AC Milan legend was an incredible striker and has been praised for his abilities to work with forwards, even if his ability as a manager have been questioned.

With a new contract, Johannsson can either stay at AZ long term or, more likely, move to a bigger club for a hefty fee soon. With Johannsson under contract, AZ can demand a bigger transfer fee from whoever comes calling, be it one of the Eredivisie’s biggest clubs of one from another country. If the 23-year-old continues scoring, and especially if he stars for the U.S., teams will definitely come calling and Johannsson could find himself on a much bigger stage before long.

AC Milan

AC Milan have officially announced on their [website](https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/media/2023-07-19/official-statement-tijjani-reijnders) the signing of Dutch midfielder Tijjani Reijnders from AZ Alkmaar on a permanent deal. The midfielder has signed a contract until the summer of 2028.

Reijnders came up in the FC Twente youth system before moving to PEC Zwolle to start his career before moving to the AZ Alkmaar U21 team. He spent a few months on loan at RKC Waalwijk before becoming a fixture in the Alkmaar first team. He has made 128 appearances for Alkmaar scoring 13 goals and providing 15 assists. He made the bulk of these appearances in the previous three seasons.

The midfielder received his first senior national call up in May 2023 but is yet to make his international debut. He has previously played for the Netherlands at the U20 level.

# Official: AC Milan Sign Dutch Midfielder From AZ Alkmaar On A Permanent Deal

A big signing for Milan to reinforce the midfield since the departure of Tonali.

Jul 20, 2023, 9:30 AM UTC

![Image 9](https://platform.acmilan.theoffside.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24798561/GalleryReijnders_2__1_.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=3.0813953488372%2C0%2C93.837209302326%2C100&w=2400)

AC Milan

AC Milan have officially announced on their [website](https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/media/2023-07-19/official-statement-tijjani-reijnders) the signing of Dutch midfielder Tijjani Reijnders from AZ Alkmaar on a permanent deal. The midfielder has signed a contract until the summer of 2028.

Reijnders came up in the FC Twente youth system before moving to PEC Zwolle to start his career before moving to the AZ Alkmaar U21 team. He spent a few months on loan at RKC Waalwijk before becoming a fixture in the Alkmaar first team. He has made 128 appearances for Alkmaar scoring 13 goals and providing 15 assists. He made the bulk of these appearances in the previous three seasons.

The midfielder received his first senior national call up in May 2023 but is yet to make his international debut. He has previously played for the Netherlands at the U20 level.

## Aron Johannsson Extends His Stay with AZ Alkmaar

 Perhaps recognizing that the grass is not always greener on the other side, Aron Johannsson will extend his stay in the Netherlands. American Soccer Now's Brian Sciaretta has the details. 

 BY  Brian Sciaretta  Posted   
 May 30, 2014   
 1:30 PM 

*    SHARE THIS STORY 
*   [![Image 3: Print_icon](http://www.americansoccernow.com/assets/print_icon.png)](http://www.americansoccernow.com/articles/aron-johannsson-extends-his-stay-with-az-alkmaar?print=true) 

*    SHARE THIS STORY 
*   [![Image 4: Print_icon](http://www.americansoccernow.com/assets/print_icon.png)](http://www.americansoccernow.com/articles/aron-johannsson-extends-his-stay-with-az-alkmaar?print=true) 

**AFTER A BREAKOUT SEASON** that saw him score 26 goals in all competitions, United States national team forward Aron Johannsson has signed a new contract with AZ Alkmaar which will run through the 2017/2018 season. Johannsson, 23, scored 17 goals in Eredivisie action along with six in the Dutch cup, two in the Europa League, and one in the Dutch Super cup for an impressive first full season in the Eredivisie. He was the league’s third leading scorer and he helped AZ to an eighth place finish.  Next year promises to be a an exciting time for the Alabama-born, Iceland-raised Johannsson as AZ Alkmaar have hired Marco Van Basten as coach. The former Dutch international enjoyed a storied playing career for Ajax and AC Milan and has since been the head coach of the Netherland’s national team, Ajax, and most recently Heerenveen.  Johannsson began his professional career with Icelandic club Fjolnir in 2009 and moved to AGF Aarhus in 2010. Following a sparkling run in 2012, he moved to AZ Alkmaar at the start of 2013. So far he has scored 65 goals at the professional level as well as two for the U.S. national team.[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx2uq1vPrqY) Johannsson is currently with the U.S. national team as it prepares for the World Cup. In the team’s first tune-up match against Azerbaijan, Johannsson came on as a second-half substitute and scored in the 81st minute en route to a 2-0 victory._Do you like Johannsson's decision to stay at Alkmaar and not go to, say, Sunderland? ## Aron Johannsson Extends His Stay with AZ Alkmaar

 Perhaps recognizing that the grass is not always greener on the other side, Aron Johannsson will extend his stay in the Netherlands. American Soccer Now's Brian Sciaretta has the details. 

 BY  Brian Sciaretta  Posted   
 May 30, 2014   
 1:30 PM 

*    SHARE THIS STORY 
*   [![Image 3: Print_icon](http://www.americansoccernow.com/assets/print_icon.png)](http://www.americansoccernow.com/articles/aron-johannsson-extends-his-stay-with-az-alkmaar?print=true)

**AFTER A BREAKOUT SEASON** that saw him score 26 goals in all competitions, United States national team forward Aron Johannsson has signed a new contract with AZ Alkmaar which will run through the 2017/2018 season. Johannsson, 23, scored 17 goals in Eredivisie action along with six in the Dutch cup, two in the Europa League, and one in the Dutch Super cup for an impressive first full season in the Eredivisie. He was the league’s third leading scorer and he helped AZ to an eighth place finish.  Next year promises to be a an exciting time for the Alabama-born, Iceland-raised Johannsson as AZ Alkmaar have hired Marco Van Basten as coach. The former Dutch international enjoyed a storied playing career for Ajax and AC Milan and has since been the head coach of the Netherland’s national team, Ajax, and most recently Heerenveen.  Johannsson began his professional career with Icelandic club Fjolnir in 2009 and moved to AGF Aarhus in 2010. Following a sparkling run in 2012, he moved to AZ Alkmaar at the start of 2013. So far he has scored 65 goals at the professional level as well as two for the U.S. national team.[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx2uq1vPrqY) Johannsson is currently with the U.S. national team as it prepares for the World Cup. In the team’s first tune-up match against Azerbaijan, Johannsson came on as a second-half substitute and scored in the 81st minute en route to a 2-0 victory._Do you like Johannsson's decision to stay at Alkmaar and not go to, say, Sunderland? # American Exports: Altidore completes move to AZ Alkmaar

![Image 3: Jozy Altidore was unveiled Wednesday by AZ Alkmaar.](https://images.mlssoccer.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_8_desktop_mobile/f_auto/prd-league/lafkm9j8tgl0l86azkfa.jpg)

Wednesday, Jul 20, 2011, 07:04 PM

![Image 4: share](https://www.mlssoccer.com/assets/images/share.png)

AMSTERDAM — United States power forward Jozy Altidore has finally completed a move to Dutch side AZ Alkmaar from Villarreal, signing a four-year deal with the _Kaasboeren_ on Wednesday.

The 21-year-old aced his medical in the afternoon after arriving on Tuesday in time to enjoy a 5-0 AZ preseason win over visiting AGOVV Apeldoorn.

Altidore had been watched by AZ technical director Earnie Stewart with a keen eye for quite a while now, and the former US star admitted to MLSsoccer.com last month that he was in advanced talks to land the young striker from Villarreal.

According to Dutch soccer magazine _Voetbal International_, the transfer deal ended up being quite complicated. AZ reportedly paid a little less than $1 million and get a portion of Altidore's salary paid by Villarreal for the next two seasons, and the Spaniards will also get a considerable percentage off any sale out of Alkmaar.

Altidore is slated to begin training under new boss Gertjan Verbeek on Thursday, AZ press officer Daan Schippers told MLSsoccer.com. The striker will be counted on to help replace the 21 league goals that departed in July with Graziano Pellè and Kolbeinn Sigthórsson.

The Cheese Farmers, who finished fourth in the Eredivisie last season, will begin their competitive schedule with a Europa league third-round qualifying tie opener at home to an opponent likely to be Czech side Jablonec on July 28. They kick off the new league campaign with a visit from PSV Eindhoven on August 7.

# American Exports: Altidore completes move to AZ Alkmaar

![Image 3: Jozy Altidore was unveiled Wednesday by AZ Alkmaar.](https://images.mlssoccer.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_8_desktop_mobile/f_auto/prd-league/lafkm9j8tgl0l86azkfa.jpg)

## Greg Seltzer

Wednesday, Jul 20, 2011, 07:04 PM

![Image 4: share](https://www.mlssoccer.com/assets/images/share.png)

*   Copy URL
*   Share on Facebook
*   [Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=American+Exports%3a+Altidore+completes+move+to+AZ+Alkmaar&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mlssoccer.com%2Fnews%2Famerican-exports-altidore-completes-move-az-alkmaar)

AMSTERDAM — United States power forward Jozy Altidore has finally completed a move to Dutch side AZ Alkmaar from Villarreal, signing a four-year deal with the _Kaasboeren_ on Wednesday.

The 21-year-old aced his medical in the afternoon after arriving on Tuesday in time to enjoy a 5-0 AZ preseason win over visiting AGOVV Apeldoorn.

Altidore had been watched by AZ technical director Earnie Stewart with a keen eye for quite a while now, and the former US star admitted to MLSsoccer.com last month that he was in advanced talks to land the young striker from Villarreal.

According to Dutch soccer magazine _Voetbal International_, the transfer deal ended up being quite complicated. AZ reportedly paid a little less than $1 million and get a portion of Altidore's salary paid by Villarreal for the next two seasons, and the Spaniards will also get a considerable percentage off any sale out of Alkmaar.

Altidore is slated to begin training under new boss Gertjan Verbeek on Thursday, AZ press officer Daan Schippers told MLSsoccer.com. The striker will be counted on to help replace the 21 league goals that departed in July with Graziano Pellè and Kolbeinn Sigthórsson.

The Cheese Farmers, who finished fourth in the Eredivisie last season, will begin their competitive schedule with a Europa league third-round qualifying tie opener at home to an opponent likely to be Czech side Jablonec on July 28. They kick off the new league campaign with a visit from PSV Eindhoven on August 7.

The **2022–23 season** was the [96th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ACF_Fiorentina_seasons "List of ACF Fiorentina seasons") in the history of [ACF Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") and their 19th consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in Serie A, the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Coppa_Italia "2022–23 Coppa Italia"), and the UEFA Europa Conference League, finishing as runners-up in the latter two competitions.

The **2022–23 season** was the [96th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ACF_Fiorentina_seasons "List of ACF Fiorentina seasons") in the history of [ACF Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina") and their 19th consecutive season in the top flight. The club participated in Serie A, the [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Coppa_Italia "2022–23 Coppa Italia"), and the UEFA Europa Conference League, finishing as runners-up in the latter two competitions.

The **2022–23 Serie A** (known as the **Serie A [TIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_Italia "Telecom Italia")** for sponsorship reasons) was the 121st season of top-tier Italian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 91st in a [round-robin tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), and the 13th since its organization under an own league committee, the [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-2)[Napoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSC_Napoli "SSC Napoli") won the title with five matches remaining after a 1–1 draw against [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") at the [Dacia Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacia_Arena "Dacia Arena") on 4 May 2023.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-4)

Napoli's title was their third league title in club history and their first since [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") led them to victory in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_Serie_A "1989–90 Serie A") — bringing an end to their 33-year _[Scudetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scudetto "Scudetto")_ drought. [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), the defending champions, finished in fourth place. It was the first time since [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000-01_Serie_A "2000-01 Serie A") that a club other than AC Milan, [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") or [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus "Juventus") had won the Serie A title.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

This year would mark the return of playoff matches for the first time since [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Serie_A "2004–05 Serie A"). If the season ends with two teams tied at the top of the league standings, those teams would play at a neutral site to determine the title winner. The match will have no [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)"), and will instead go directly to a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") should the teams be tied after regulation. Head-to-head will still will used as a tiebreaker elsewhere on the board.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-5)

The [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") in February announced their intention to run a tournament in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") during the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), consisting of players who were not called up to play for the [men's national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). The unusual scheduling of the World Cup in [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") forced many leagues to interrupt their seasons for weeks, so the Serie A saw this as an opportunity to bolster its image abroad while keeping its players active.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-6) The idea received mixed feedback, and was ultimately cancelled by the league due to logistical and funding issues.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-7)

In January 2023, the Serie A deducted 15 points from [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") after an investigation by the [FIGC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Football_Federation "Italian Football Federation") accused the club of manipulating their balancing sheets to show false gains of around 60m euros. Months later in April, Italy's highest court ordered the case to be re-examined, and the points were restored. The original ruling was upheld—though this time resulting in Juventus being docked 10 points—in May 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-8)

On 28 July 2023, [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") released a statement confirming Juventus has violated finance regulations.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-9) Consequently, Juventus faced penalties including exclusion from the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-10)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

[Cremonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cremonese "US Cremonese") returned to the [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") for the first time in 26 years—their longest absence from the top league in history. [Lecce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Lecce "US Lecce") returned after two years. [Monza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Monza "AC Monza") were promoted for the first time in the club's history, making them the 67th team to play at the highest level of Italian football.

[Cagliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagliari_Calcio "Cagliari Calcio") were relegated to the [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") after six years, while [Venezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezia_FC "Venezia FC") were relegated after only one. [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C. "Genoa C.F.C.") were relegated after 15 seasons, thus ending the club's longest consecutive run in the top league.

This was the first season since the [2003–04 campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Serie_A "2003–04 Serie A") without any representation from the [archipelagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of Italy (teams located on [Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardinia "Sardinia") or [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily")) in the Serie A.

The **2022–23 Serie A** (known as the **Serie A [TIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_Italia "Telecom Italia")** for sponsorship reasons) was the 121st season of top-tier Italian [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 91st in a [round-robin tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament"), and the 13th since its organization under an own league committee, the [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-2)[Napoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSC_Napoli "SSC Napoli") won the title with five matches remaining after a 1–1 draw against [Udinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio") at the [Dacia Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacia_Arena "Dacia Arena") on 4 May 2023.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-4)

Napoli's title was their third league title in club history and their first since [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") led them to victory in [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_Serie_A "1989–90 Serie A") — bringing an end to their 33-year _[Scudetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scudetto "Scudetto")_ drought. [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan"), the defending champions, finished in fourth place. It was the first time since [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") in [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000-01_Serie_A "2000-01 Serie A") that a club other than AC Milan, [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") or [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus "Juventus") had won the Serie A title.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

This year would mark the return of playoff matches for the first time since [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Serie_A "2004–05 Serie A"). If the season ends with two teams tied at the top of the league standings, those teams would play at a neutral site to determine the title winner. The match will have no [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)"), and will instead go directly to a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") should the teams be tied after regulation. Head-to-head will still will used as a tiebreaker elsewhere on the board.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-5)

The [Lega Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") in February announced their intention to run a tournament in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") during the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), consisting of players who were not called up to play for the [men's national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team"). The unusual scheduling of the World Cup in [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") forced many leagues to interrupt their seasons for weeks, so the Serie A saw this as an opportunity to bolster its image abroad while keeping its players active.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-6) The idea received mixed feedback, and was ultimately cancelled by the league due to logistical and funding issues.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-7)

In January 2023, the Serie A deducted 15 points from [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") after an investigation by the [FIGC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Football_Federation "Italian Football Federation") accused the club of manipulating their balancing sheets to show false gains of around 60m euros. Months later in April, Italy's highest court ordered the case to be re-examined, and the points were restored. The original ruling was upheld—though this time resulting in Juventus being docked 10 points—in May 2023.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-8)

On 28 July 2023, [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") released a statement confirming Juventus has violated finance regulations.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-9) Consequently, Juventus faced penalties including exclusion from the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A#cite_note-10)

## Teams

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Serie_A&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Teams")]

[Cremonese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Cremonese "US Cremonese") returned to the [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") for the first time in 26 years—their longest absence from the top league in history. [Lecce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Lecce "US Lecce") returned after two years. [Monza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Monza "AC Monza") were promoted for the first time in the club's history, making them the 67th team to play at the highest level of Italian football.

[Cagliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagliari_Calcio "Cagliari Calcio") were relegated to the [Serie B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_B "Serie B") after six years, while [Venezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezia_FC "Venezia FC") were relegated after only one. [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C. "Genoa C.F.C.") were relegated after 15 seasons, thus ending the club's longest consecutive run in the top league.

This was the first season since the [2003–04 campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003%E2%80%9304_Serie_A "2003–04 Serie A") without any representation from the [archipelagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of Italy (teams located on [Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardinia "Sardinia") or [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily")) in the Serie A.

The **2022–23 Serie A** (known as the **Serie A TIM** for sponsorship reasons) was the 121st season of top-tier Italian [football](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 91st in a round-robin tournament, and the 13th since its organization under an own league committee, the [Lega Serie A](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A"). [AC Milan](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") were the defending champions.

On 4 May 2023, [Napoli](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/S.S.C._Napoli "S.S.C. Napoli") secured their third Serie A title and the first since 1990 with five matches to spare, following a 1–1 draw away to [Udinese](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio").

## Summary[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2022%25E2%2580%259323_Serie_A%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Starting from the 2022–23 season, should the first and second, or 17th and 18th-placed teams at the end of the season be tied on points, a play-off tiebreaker match would be held at a neutral site to determine the title and final team relegated respectively. The tiebreaker would not have extra time, and would instead directly go to a [penalty shoot-out](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out "Penalty shoot-out") should the two teams be tied after 90 minutes. This was the first time play-offs were used since the [2004–05 campaign](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Serie_A "2004–05 Serie A").

[Lega Serie A](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") had initially planned to run a tournament featuring Serie A teams in the [United States](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/United_States "United States") during the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), but this was later cancelled.

In January 2023, Juventus were deducted 15 points as punishment for capital gain violations. In April 2023, the decision was overturned and Juventus were given those points back. However, following a new investigation, Juventus were docked 10 points in May 2023.

On 28 July 2023, [UEFA](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") released a statement confirming Juventus' violation of the financial regulations. Consequently, Juventus faced penalties including exclusion from the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").

The **2022–23 Serie A** (known as the **Serie A TIM** for sponsorship reasons) was the 121st season of top-tier Italian [football](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), the 91st in a round-robin tournament, and the 13th since its organization under an own league committee, the [Lega Serie A](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A"). [AC Milan](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") were the defending champions.

On 4 May 2023, [Napoli](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/S.S.C._Napoli "S.S.C. Napoli") secured their third Serie A title and the first since 1990 with five matches to spare, following a 1–1 draw away to [Udinese](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Udinese_Calcio "Udinese Calcio").

## Summary[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Ffootball.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2F2022%25E2%2580%259323_Serie_A%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Starting from the 2022–23 season, should the first and second, or 17th and 18th-placed teams at the end of the season be tied on points, a play-off tiebreaker match would be held at a neutral site to determine the title and final team relegated respectively. The tiebreaker would not have extra time, and would instead directly go to a [penalty shoot-out](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out "Penalty shoot-out") should the two teams be tied after 90 minutes. This was the first time play-offs were used since the [2004–05 campaign](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Serie_A "2004–05 Serie A").

[Lega Serie A](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Lega_Serie_A "Lega Serie A") had initially planned to run a tournament featuring Serie A teams in the [United States](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/United_States "United States") during the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), but this was later cancelled.

In January 2023, Juventus were deducted 15 points as punishment for capital gain violations. In April 2023, the decision was overturned and Juventus were given those points back. However, following a new investigation, Juventus were docked 10 points in May 2023.

On 28 July 2023, [UEFA](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") released a statement confirming Juventus' violation of the financial regulations. Consequently, Juventus faced penalties including exclusion from the [2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Europa_Conference_League "2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League").

[Cagliari](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Cagliari_Calcio "Cagliari Calcio") were relegated after six years in the top flight, [Genoa](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Genoa_C.F.C. "Genoa C.F.C.") relegated to second level after 15 years, and [Venezia](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Venezia_F.C. "Venezia F.C.") relegated after only one year in the top flight. They were replaced by [Lecce](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/U.S._Lecce "U.S. Lecce"), Serie B champions, [Cremonese](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/U.S._Cremonese "U.S. Cremonese"), Serie B runners-up, and [Monza](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/A.C._Monza "A.C. Monza"), Serie B playoff winners. Lecce returned to top flight after 2 years of absence, whilst Cremonese returned after 26 years of absence and Monza were promoted to Serie A for the first time in the club's history.

# AZ move closer to their own transfer record and suddenly have their desired reinforcement in place

[Transfers](https://www.goal.com/en/category/transfers/1/k94w8e1yy9ch14mllpf4srnks)

[AZ Alkmaar](https://www.goal.com/en/team/az-alkmaar/3kfktv64h7kg7zryax1wktr5r)

****AZ have signed a new midfielder. The Alkmaar club are paying seven million euros to FC Midtjylland for the services of Valdemar Byskov, according to the Danish outlet Bold.****

Valdemar Byskov is a 21-year-old central midfielder who came through Midtjylland's youth academy and has played youth internationals for Denmark Under-21s.



Already, Byskov has made more than 100 appearances for the Danish club's first team. He has scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists.

After the weekend, Byskov will travel to the Netherlands to undergo a medical. He will then sign a long-term contract at the AFAS Stadion.

[Europa League ![Image 26: Sunderland crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/hRMDFkwiIhvjfGNfMkNk_.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) Sunderland SUN 16 Sept 2026 12:00 ![Image 27: AZ Alkmaar crest](https://cdn.sportfeeds.io/sdl/images/team/crest/medium/X963ylMA_nSxn3F6AOvrP.png?quality=60&auto=webp&format=pjpg) AZ Alkmaar AZ](https://www.goal.com/en/match/sunderland-vs-az-alkmaar/WlL41_PTybnOP6WCtbpwW)

According to Bold, AZ are paying 'around seven million euros' for the talented playmaker. That makes Byskov one of the most expensive signings in the club's history.

Still, the most expensive signing remains Weslley Patati. AZ signed him from Maccabi Tel Aviv last summer for 7.3 million euros.

AZ Alkmaar striker joins FC Utrecht on loan with purchase option included

[Get Belgian and Dutch Football News](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/)

Fri, Aug 28, 2026·

1 min read

[FC Utrecht](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/fc-utrecht-bring-in-norwegian-winger-on-loan-from-lille/) have announced the signing of Sem van Duijn from [AZ Alkmaar](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/az-alkmaar-set-to-reunite-with-calvin-stengs/) on loan for the 2026/2027 Eredivisie season. The 22-year-old striker has a year in which to convince Utrecht to pick up the purchase option they have agreed with AZ Alkmaar as part of the loan deal. Van Duijn gets to link back up with former Telstar head coach Antonio Correia, who left the side to take over at Utrecht this summer.

Van Duijn made a name for himself in the amateur leagues with Quick Boys. Prior to joining AZ Alkmaar in 2024, he scored 22 goals in 70 games for the side, with 19 of these coming in 38 games during the 2023/2024 season. The striker only played two games for the AZ Alkmaar senior team, with most of his time spent with Jong AZ Alkmaar in the second tier. Over the course of two seasons he scored 15 goals for the side in 43 games.

Van Duijn had a successful spell on loan at Telstar with Correia last season. In 16 games for the then newly promoted side he scored five goals and provided two assists.

AZ Alkmaar striker joins FC Utrecht on loan with purchase option included

[Get Belgian and Dutch Football News](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/)

Fri, Aug 28, 2026·

1 min read

[FC Utrecht](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/fc-utrecht-bring-in-norwegian-winger-on-loan-from-lille/) have announced the signing of Sem van Duijn from [AZ Alkmaar](https://getfootballnewsbene.com/az-alkmaar-set-to-reunite-with-calvin-stengs/) on loan for the 2026/2027 Eredivisie season. The 22-year-old striker has a year in which to convince Utrecht to pick up the purchase option they have agreed with AZ Alkmaar as part of the loan deal. Van Duijn gets to link back up with former Telstar head coach Antonio Correia, who left the side to take over at Utrecht this summer.

Van Duijn made a name for himself in the amateur leagues with Quick Boys. Prior to joining AZ Alkmaar in 2024, he scored 22 goals in 70 games for the side, with 19 of these coming in 38 games during the 2023/2024 season. The striker only played two games for the AZ Alkmaar senior team, with most of his time spent with Jong AZ Alkmaar in the second tier. Over the course of two seasons he scored 15 goals for the side in 43 games.

Van Duijn had a successful spell on loan at Telstar with Correia last season. In 16 games for the then newly promoted side he scored five goals and provided two assists.

**Mees de Wit** (born 17 April 1998) is a Dutch professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-back "Left-back") for [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") club [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mees_de_Wit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

De Wit made his [Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eerste_Divisie "Eerste Divisie") debut for [Jong Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jong_Ajax "Jong Ajax") on 25 August 2017 in a game against [Fortuna Sittard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Sittard "Fortuna Sittard").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-1) He signed for Sporting's U-23 team for the 2018–19 season on 19 July 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-2) On 11 March 2019, Stefano van Delden, De Wit's agent in 2017 and 2018, made the news as he was suspected of threatening different members of the [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") board on several occasions during the period from 26 October 2017 to 25 September 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-3)

On 20 January 2020, de Wit moved to Spanish club [Orihuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orihuela_CF "Orihuela CF") on loan for the rest of the season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-4)

On 6 July 2021, he returned to the Netherlands and signed a contract with [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") for two years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-5)

De Wit performed exceptionally while playing for PEC Zwolle, leading to a five-year contract with [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") starting in July 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-6)

**Mees de Wit** (born 17 April 1998) is a Dutch professional [footballer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [left-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-back "Left-back") for [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") club [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mees_de_Wit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]

De Wit made his [Eerste Divisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eerste_Divisie "Eerste Divisie") debut for [Jong Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jong_Ajax "Jong Ajax") on 25 August 2017 in a game against [Fortuna Sittard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortuna_Sittard "Fortuna Sittard").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-1) He signed for Sporting's U-23 team for the 2018–19 season on 19 July 2018.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-2) On 11 March 2019, Stefano van Delden, De Wit's agent in 2017 and 2018, made the news as he was suspected of threatening different members of the [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") board on several occasions during the period from 26 October 2017 to 25 September 2018.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-3)

On 20 January 2020, de Wit moved to Spanish club [Orihuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orihuela_CF "Orihuela CF") on loan for the rest of the season.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-4)

On 6 July 2021, he returned to the Netherlands and signed a contract with [PEC Zwolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEC_Zwolle "PEC Zwolle") for two years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-5)

De Wit performed exceptionally while playing for PEC Zwolle, leading to a five-year contract with [AZ Alkmaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AZ_Alkmaar "AZ Alkmaar") starting in July 2022.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mees_de_Wit#cite_note-6)
